edges.effect_quant: The strongest disorder-specific synthesis now comes from the 2024 JAMA Psychiatry network meta-analysis, where CBT reduced GAD severity versus treatment as usual (SMD -0.74, 95% CI -1.09 to -0.38) and remained superior at 3 to 12 months (SMD -0.60, 95% CI -0.99 to -0.21).
edges.population: adults with primary generalized anxiety disorder treated in outpatient or remote psychotherapy trials
edges.mechanism: CBT for GAD targets chronic worry through cognitive restructuring, behavioral experiments, exposure to uncertainty, and alternative coping strategies. By reducing avoidance of uncertainty and interrupting repetitive worry loops, it tends to lower both subjective distress and clinician-rated GAD severity.
edges.summary: This is one of the cleaner psychotherapy edges in the graph. Disorder-specific evidence repeatedly shows CBT meaningfully reduces GAD severity, with benefits that often persist after treatment ends.
edges.caveats: Different CBT packages vary in focus, delivery format, and comparator strength. Remote or low-intensity formats can be helpful, but the strongest evidence still tends to favor therapist-delivered individual or group CBT.
